title: Outpouring of love, money for kids left motherless by cancer - NewsBreak
text:
By Melissa Moon ,
3 hours ago MEMPHIS, Tenn. -- Two local Kiwanis Clubs and members of the community are making sure the children who lost their young mother to cancer have what they need in the years to come.
There were hugs all around in Timera Allen's home Wednesday when the Kiwanis Club of Millington gave her a $500 check to help care for five nieces, from ages 2 to 16.
The girls' mother, Kerrie Rayford, lost her battle with cancer last month at the age of 34.
Support needed for children after mother dies from cancer Children left behind after young mom dies from cancer. Courtesy: Timara Allen Members of the Kiwanis Club of Bluff City were also there. The volunteer organization has donated hundreds of dollars worth of school supplies and uniforms to ensure the older girls attend school.
The president of the organization, who showed up in an ice cream truck for the kids, said their organization is committed to providing school supplies and uniforms for the girls for at least the next five years.
"It's something that we were not prepared for as far as losing her. It happened so fast. So, this really helps them a lot," said the children's grandmother.
Local Kiwanis clubs surprise Ratford's kids with ice cream and money. Courtesy: Kiwanis Club of Bluff City Allen told WREG there wasn’t anything she wouldn’t do for her sister, and raising her five daughters with the help of her mother feels like a gift.
Since she shared their story, her GoFundMe has raised nearly $16,000 for the children.
Kiwanis Club of Bluff City said it is providing Allen with a financial planner because she wants to put the money in a trust for her nieces.
The club is also planning to help the older girls obtain volunteer hours they may need for college.
"I appreciate everything," said Allen.
Kiwanis International is a global organization of volunteers focused on community service and dedicated to improving the world one child and community at a time.
The local Kiwanis groups said this is their mission and why they agreed to help this family.
